import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_excel('census_cps_median_household_income_by_state.xlsx', sheet_name='h08', header=None)
# Current dollars section starts at row 7
# Row 10 is United States (first occurrence)
us_row = df[df[0].astype(str).str.strip() == 'United States'].iloc[0]
# Years: 2025 (col 1/B), 2024 (col 3/D), 2023 (col 5/F), 2022 (col 7/H), 2021 (col 9/J)
vals = [float(us_row[c]) for c in [1, 3, 5, 7, 9]]
result = sum(vals) / len(vals)

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_excel('census_cps_median_household_income_by_state.xlsx', sheet_name='h08', header=None)
# Constant dollars section: second occurrence of United States (row 65, index 64)
us_constant = df[df[0].astype(str).str.strip() == 'United States'].iloc[1]
# Mapping of years to columns: 2022: H (col 7), 2021: J (col 9), 2020: L (col 11), 2019: N (col 13), 2018: P (col 15)
year_cols = {'2022': 7, '2021': 9, '2020': 11, '2019': 13, '2018': 15}
result = max(year_cols.keys(), key=lambda y: float(us_constant[year_cols[y]]))

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_excel('census_cps_median_household_income_by_state.xlsx', sheet_name='h08', header=None)
states = ['California', 'Florida', 'Illinois', 'New York', 'Texas']
count = 0
for state in states:
    val = float(df[df[0].astype(str).str.strip() == state].iloc[0][1])
    if val >= 80000:
        count += 1
result = count
